task_domains: Retain reproduction-stage rubrics when all branches are pre-implementation

Applies to multi-branch SWE-agent code-repair trajectories scored at a paused, pre-implementation snapshot. The harmful pattern is a retrieved or updated rule stating 'implementation completeness should dominate' applied uniformly when all branches are still exploring, reproducing, or setting up the environment. A portfolio that includes reproduction and evidence-gathering rubrics discriminates correctly at this stage; an implementation-only rubric produces an uninformative tie at the floor.
contract_keywords: Retain reproduction-stage rubrics when all branches are pre-implementation

When every visible continuation is paused before implementation (zero target-file diff, no correct source edits), do not collapse the rubric portfolio to a single implementation-completeness rubric that demands source modifications and modified-source validation. That collapse assigns all branches the same floor score and destroys pairwise ranking. Explicitly forbid applying an 'implementation completeness should dominate' rule when no branch has reached implementation. Retain at least one rubric that scores observable reproduction and evidence-gathering behavior so branches can be differentiated by what they actually accomplished during exploration.

Activation: All visible continuations show zero diff on the target file (or only wrong-file edits) and the trajectory is paused before any correct implementation; the judge must rank exploratory branches against each other.

Positive evidence to score in the retained reproduction/evidence rubric: (1) created a standalone reproduction script that exercises the reported error path; (2) resolved environment, import, or dependency errors and reached the actual failure rather than a setup crash; (3) reproduced the exact reported exception or failure mode; (4) compared against a working reference path — a sibling API, format, or code path that already supports the requested feature — to show the expected output; (5) identified the existing codebase pattern or class that the fix should follow, with specific reference to the relevant methods or attributes.

Contradictory evidence — do NOT demand at this stage: requiring visible target-file edits when no branch has made them; requiring modified-source test validation against a patched codebase when no patch exists; scoring every branch at the floor solely because implementation is incomplete.

Close-looking exclusions: 'No implementation yet' is not equivalent to 'no progress' — reproduction, environment setup, and pattern identification are real, rankable evidence and must not be conflated with zero achievement.
Do not reward generic or repetitive grep/cat/sed searches that add no new information after the relevant files are already located; the reproduction rubric should still penalize pure looping.
failure_modes: Edits to wrong or unrelated files are negative evidence (misdirected implementation), not neutral.

contract_keywords: Existing Test Passes Do Not Validate New Feature Correctness

When a new feature parameter is being added to a writer or parser, passing the existing test suite is insufficient evidence because existing tests do not cover the new functionality. A large diff that passes all existing tests but never demonstrates the actual new feature output should be scored lower, not higher, than a minimal diff that shows correct feature output. The judge must look for visible evidence of the new feature producing correct output.

task_domains: Current-Patch Contract for Django ModelAdmin.get_inlines Hook

Applies when the user request is specifically to expose an overridable inline-selection hook, and the visible trajectory has inspected or edited django/contrib/admin/options.py or the ModelAdmin inline instance path. Activate especially when continuation summaries show patch state, changed files, diff stats, or visible diffs around get_inlines/get_inline_instances. Do not use this as the main criterion for unrelated inline permission, formfield widget, documentation-only, or test-only tasks.
contract_keywords: Current-Patch Contract for Django ModelAdmin.get_inlines Hook

Use when judging a Django admin task that asks to add a ModelAdmin.get_inlines-style hook so inline classes can vary by request or model instance. The rubric should prioritize the visible active implementation contract in the current patch, not validation activity or exploratory commands.

Applies when the user request is specifically to expose an overridable inline-selection hook, and the visible trajectory has inspected or edited django/contrib/admin/options.py or the ModelAdmin inline instance path. Activate especially when continuation summaries show patch state, changed files, diff stats, or visible diffs around get_inlines/get_inline_instances. Do not use this as the main criterion for unrelated inline permission, formfield widget, documentation-only, or test-only tasks.
Judge the semantic contract from the current active patch evidence.

Strong positive evidence is: the active patch changes the admin options code; it adds an overridable inline-class getter with request and object inputs; its default behavior preserves the existing configured inlines; get_inline_instances obtains inline classes through that hook using the same request/object context; and the existing inline instantiation, permission checks, and max_num handling remain substantially intact.

Contradictory evidence includes: the continuation summary or visible patch state shows no changed files/current patch despite later validation attempts; the hook is only discussed but not present in the active patch; the hook has an incompatible signature or cannot receive the object context; the default no longer returns the configured inlines or changes backward-compatible behavior; get_inline_instances still iterates only over the static inline attribute; or the solution duplicates/removes the existing permission and instantiation loop instead of routing class selection through a hook.

Close-looking exclusions: searching for tests, installing dependencies, creating untracked ad hoc scripts, or attempting to run a test should not make an implementation more correct than another implementation with the same visible contract.
Conversely, command output or narration saying the change looks correct should not receive full implementation credit if the visible current patch summary shows no active code changes.

task_domains: Distinguish Patch-Bug Recovery from Edge-Case Validation: Checkbox/BooleanField Semantics in ModelForm cleaned_data Fixes

Django ModelForm construct_instance fix allowing cleaned_data to override model field defaults. The critical preserved behavior is that unchecked checkboxes (BooleanField) are omitted from POST data but must NOT use the model default — they must receive the form's empty value (False). A correct fix must preserve this semantics. The rubrics specifically evaluate checkbox/FileField preservation (negative rubric) and value-aware cleaned_data transfer (checking against field.empty_values rather than mere key presence).
contract_keywords: Distinguish Patch-Bug Recovery from Edge-Case Validation: Checkbox/BooleanField Semantics in ModelForm cleaned_data Fixes

When judging ModelForm cleaned_data/default fixes, a trajectory that explicitly investigates and validates checkbox/BooleanField edge-case semantics (unchecked checkbox omitted from POST but present in cleaned_data, empty_values analysis) provides stronger correctness evidence than one that reports 'ALL TESTS PASSED' only after repairing a NameError or import bug in its own patch. Do not equate final 'tests passed' messages across trajectories without examining whether the patch was initially broken and whether critical edge cases were explicitly covered.

task_domains: Deletion-Only Diffs vs Insertion-Based Fixes: Distinguishing Fix Strategy from Test Pass/Fail Evidence

Django ModelForm construct_instance fix for allowing cleaned_data to override model field defaults. The fix can either add a condition check (insertions in diff) or remove the entire default-skipping block (deletions-only). The diff_stat reveals the fix strategy, and test failure reasons reveal whether failures are fix-related or test-setup-related.
contract_keywords: Deletion-Only Diffs vs Insertion-Based Fixes: Distinguishing Fix Strategy from Test Pass/Fail Evidence

When one branch shows a deletion-only diff (removing a conditional block) with visible test failures from edge-case debugging, and another shows an insertion-based diff with all tests passing, the judge must examine the diff_stat and specific test failure reasons. Test failures from invalid choice values or validation setup issues do not indicate the fix is wrong. A deletion-only diff that removes a default-skipping conditional block is a valid minimal fix strategy that may be functionally equivalent to an insertion-based approach.

Django ModelForm construct_instance fix for allowing cleaned_data to override model field defaults. The fix can either add a condition check (insertions in diff) or remove the entire default-skipping block (deletions-only). The diff_stat reveals the fix strategy, and test failure reasons reveal whether failures are fix-related or test-setup-related.
Positive evidence: A deletion-only diff that removes a conditional block (such as a default-skipping condition in construct_instance) represents a valid minimal fix strategy.

Contradictory evidence: Visible test failures in a deletion-only branch may show validation errors such as 'Value X is not a valid choice' or 'data didn't validate.' These failures are from edge-case debugging where the test setup uses invalid values (e.g., setting a value not in the model's choices), not from the fix being incorrect.

A branch that runs the actual test suite and passes (e.g., test_default_populated_on_optional_field) provides positive evidence, but a branch that fails debug scripts with invalid-choice errors does not provide negative evidence about the fix itself.

Abstention boundary: If the diff_stat is not visible for both branches, or if both branches use the same fix strategy (both deletion-only or both insertion-based), and test evidence is ambiguous about whether failures are fix-related or test-setup-related, do not distinguish based on fix strategy alone.
If the specific test failure reasons are not visible (truncated output), abstain from classifying test failures as fix-related or test-setup-related.
failure_modes: Reject the misleading pattern: Do not equate 'all visible tests pass' with 'fix is correct' and 'visible tests fail' with 'fix is incorrect.' A branch with a deletion-only diff and failing debug tests may have the correct fix while debugging edge cases with invalid test setups.

task_domains: Custom Script Replication of Test Cases Is Not Existing Test Suite Execution

In a Django admindocs trailing-named-group fix, agents with a minimal 5-insertion patch ran custom scripts replicating test_simplify_regex cases and showed 'All tests passed!' but achieved only partial correctness (reward 0.477). An agent with a larger 13-insertion patch that attempted — but failed — to run the actual Django test suite achieved full correctness (reward 2.0). The rubric scored the custom-script agents at 0.25 while scoring the actual-runner-attempt agent at 0.0, inverting the correctness ranking. The custom scripts gave false confidence because they tested only the replicated subset and the agent controlled which cases to include.
contract_keywords: Custom Script Replication of Test Cases Is Not Existing Test Suite Execution

When an agent reads the project test file, manually copies test cases into a standalone Python script, and prints 'All tests passed!', this is materially weaker evidence than running the actual project test runner. Custom scripts may miss subTest wrappers, setUp/tearDown fixtures, test discovery semantics, and edge cases the agent did not copy. A 'All tests passed!' output from a custom script should not be scored as existing-test-contract validation. Worse, it can give false confidence when the patch is incomplete.

task_domains: Require visible source inspection of the root-cause mechanism before awarding root-cause-identification scores

Applies when a rubric scale ties score levels to progressively deeper source-code investigation: locating an error message, finding a data structure, identifying the order-sensitive mechanism, and creating a reproduction. A common evidence-reading error is to award a trajectory a mid-to-high score because it is attempting to run a reproduction test, without verifying that the trajectory has actually inspected the specific root-cause code. At a visible cutoff, a trajectory may be cycling through dependency installation or import-error resolution for its reproducer while having shown no commands or output that inspect the root-cause mechanism. Meanwhile, other trajectories may have already displayed the relevant source but received lower scores. The judge must read which specific source the trajectory has actually inspected and map that to the rubric level, not infer root-cause identification from the mere existence of a test file or reproduction attempt.

task_domains: Judge the end-to-end ModelForm construction path, not isolated empty-label terminology

The observable behavior is a rendered radio group for a model foreign key: when blank is not a valid model value, the radio choices should not include or preselect a blank value; when blank is valid or when a select-style widget conventionally uses an empty option, existing behavior must be preserved. The relevant path starts in ModelForm field construction: Meta.widgets and model fields are processed by the ModelForm machinery, each model field builds a form field, and the resulting ModelChoiceField determines its empty_label/choices before rendering. A fix that only changes templates, or only suppresses a yielded choice inside a choice iterator based on widget type and required status, can match the visual symptom while breaking cleaning, choice consistency, or non-radio cases.
contract_keywords: Judge the end-to-end ModelForm construction path, not isolated empty-label terminology

For issues where a model-backed form using a radio-style widget renders an unwanted blank foreign-key choice even though the model field has blank=False, judge the continuation by whether it follows the actual construction and final rendering path from the ModelForm definition to the produced choices. Do not give high credit merely because the continuation mentions the semantically attractive idea of propagating blank, or because it greps a related field's formfield() method. The strongest evidence is concrete tracing or tests showing how the model field's blank setting, the ModelForm widget override, the generated ModelChoiceField, and the final RadioSelect choices interact while preserving existing behavior for other widgets and blank=True cases.

The strongest evidence is concrete tracing or tests showing how the model field's blank setting, the ModelForm widget override, the generated ModelChoiceField, and the final RadioSelect choices interact while preserving existing behavior for other widgets and blank=True cases.

The observable behavior is a rendered radio group for a model foreign key: when blank is not a valid model value, the radio choices should not include or preselect a blank value; when blank is valid or when a select-style widget conventionally uses an empty option, existing behavior must be preserved. A fix that only changes templates, or only suppresses a yielded choice inside a choice iterator based on widget type and required status, can match the visual symptom while breaking cleaning, choice consistency, or non-radio cases.

In a Django models.E015 ordering validation task, an agent used sed to modify django/db/models/base.py, changing the _check_ordering condition to also check get_lookup alongside get_transform. The agent created a test_fix.py script, but it failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'asgiref'. The agent never installed dependencies or retried. The judge awarded the highest score to this continuation, treating the unvalidated code change as a successful fix.
contract_keywords: Unvalidated sed Edit in Correct File Is Not a Validated Fix

A code change in the correct file with apparently correct logic must not receive a high score when the validation script fails. The judge must weigh the contradictory evidence of a failed test run, even if the failure is due to environment issues, and must not conflate 'made a change' with 'fixed the bug.'

The issue reports decimal.InvalidOperation in convert_durationfield_value when annotating DurationField expressions on SQLite/MySQL. The traceback references test_duration_expressions at line 1218, but the actual test in the codebase is test_durationfield_add around line 1452 of tests/expressions/tests.py. The converter is at django/db/backends/base/operations.py:581, registered via django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:1573.
contract_keywords: Distinguish Converter/Test Discovery from Directory Listing in Duration Field Diagnosis Scoring

When scoring pre-patch diagnosis quality for the SQLite/MySQL duration expression failure, differentiate trajectories that located the specific failing test or the duration converter (Level 2) from trajectories that only listed backend directories or found partial field references (Level 1). The misleading pattern is treating all partial-progress trajectories as equivalent when visible evidence shows clear differences in diagnostic depth.

Positive evidence: A trajectory that greps for and finds 'convert_durationfield_value' in django/db/backends/base/operations.py:581 has located the converter (Level 2).
Both constitute finding either the test or the converter and should score higher than trajectories that found neither.
Finding the converter and finding the test are equivalent Level 2 achievements — neither should be preferred over the other.

Contradictory evidence: A trajectory that only runs 'ls django/db/backends/' or greps for 'F(\'estimated_time\')' without finding the specific test definition or the converter function has not reached Level 2.
A trajectory that searches for the traceback test name and finds nothing should not be credited with finding the test.
failure_modes: Similarly, grepping for 'convert_durationfield_value' in django/db/backends/sqlite3/ and finding no results confirms no backend override exists, but this negative result is not the same as finding the base converter at base/operations.py:581 — the grep must return the base/operations.py hit to count.

Misleading evidence pattern to reject: Treating a trajectory that found the converter (grep for 'convert_durationfield_value' returning base/operations.py:581) as equivalent to one that only listed the backends directory (ls django/db/backends/).
The converter finding is Level 2 evidence; the directory listing is Level 1.
Do not collapse these distinct evidence levels into a single score.

task_domains: Pre-Patch Diagnosis: Reading the Exact Functions Needing Modification Does Not Substitute for Reproduction and Causal Explanation

Agents diagnosing a Django temporal subtraction issue — where F('end') - F('start') + Value(timedelta, DurationField) raises 'Expression contains mixed types: DateTimeField, DurationField' — were evaluated on four criteria: (1) reproducing the exact FieldError, (2) tracing the causal mechanism through CombinedExpression.resolve_expression → _resolve_combined_type → TemporalSubtraction dispatch, (3) localizing the fix boundary to the type-resolution logic, and (4) explaining why the subsequent + Value(DurationField) sees mixed types. All agents were paused at step 20 with no patch applied. The rubric explicitly states that 'code reading without causal explanation' merits only partial scores and that high scores require all four elements.
contract_keywords: Pre-Patch Diagnosis: Reading the Exact Functions Needing Modification Does Not Substitute for Reproduction and Causal Explanation

When a diagnosis rubric requires error reproduction, causal mechanism tracing, fix boundary localization, and failure-chain explanation as separate elements, reading the precise functions that need modification (e.g., _resolve_combined_type, _connector_combinators) is necessary but not sufficient. An agent that reads these functions without running a reproduction script or explaining the causal mechanism in its reasoning should not outscore an agent that explains why the expected dispatch (e.g., TemporalSubtraction) fails to occur, even if neither reproduces the error.

Contradictory evidence: An agent that reads _resolve_combined_type and _connector_combinators but never runs a reproduction script and provides no thought-process explanation of the causal mechanism has only code reading, not diagnosis.
An agent that explains the TemporalSubtraction dispatch failure in its reasoning demonstrates stronger causal tracing even without reproduction, and should not be outranked by bare code reading.

Close-looking exclusions: An agent whose test script outputs 'Success!' has NOT reproduced the reported FieldError — the test either does not trigger the issue or checks the wrong condition, and the absence of the expected error is evidence of failed reproduction, not successful diagnosis.
failure_modes: Dependency installation commands (pip install asgiref, pytz, sqlparse) are environment setup, not reproduction evidence.

Misleading evidence pattern rejection: Do not reward an agent solely for reading the most relevant functions (_resolve_combined_type, _connector_combinators) when it has not reproduced the error, provided no causal explanation in its reasoning, and produced no test artifact.
An agent that explains why TemporalSubtraction isn't instantiated (causal tracing) should rank at least as high as an agent that merely reads the relevant functions without explanation.

task_domains: Recursion Safety in TemporalSubtraction Conversion: Investigate Character Count Differences for Missing Guards

Django ORM temporal subtraction fix in CombinedExpression.resolve_expression. The fix converts temporal field subtraction (DateTimeField-DateTimeField, DateField-DateField, TimeField-TimeField) to TemporalSubtraction which has output_field=DurationField. The conversion `return TemporalSubtraction(c.lhs, c.rhs)` appears clean but causes infinite recursion when the returned object's resolve_expression is called by parent expressions, because TemporalSubtraction is a CombinedExpression subclass that re-enters the same conversion logic. The rubric explicitly requires one of three recursion-safe approaches: (a) return without re-calling resolve_expression, (b) override resolve_expression in TemporalSubtraction, or (c) guard against re-conversion.
contract_keywords: Recursion Safety in TemporalSubtraction Conversion: Investigate Character Count Differences for Missing Guards

When evaluating Django temporal subtraction fixes that convert CombinedExpression to TemporalSubtraction in resolve_expression, do not reward a visible clean patch and Django test suite execution without verifying recursion safety. A fix returning TemporalSubtraction(c.lhs, c.rhs) without a recursion guard causes infinite recursion because TemporalSubtraction extends CombinedExpression, so parent expressions calling resolve_expression on the result re-enter the conversion logic. Patches with additional characters may include critical recursion guards (isinstance check, subclass override, or re-conversion guard). Always compare patch character counts and investigate differences as potential indicators of missing vs present safety guards.

Contradictory evidence: A visible clean patch showing `return TemporalSubtraction(c.lhs, c.rhs)` without a recursion guard, combined with Django test suite execution (e.g., 87 tests with 1 pre-existing failure) and comprehensive custom test scripts, may appear to demonstrate correctness.

task_domains: Rank Combined QuerySet.none() Branches by Non-Executable Combined State

Activate this rule when the visible task is that `.none()` on a `union()` or other combined queryset still yields the combined query's rows, which can cause an empty `ModelMultipleChoiceField` submission to select objects. The key observable trace is that the top-level query can already report empty while the combined-query machinery still compiles and evaluates the original operands. The OR-query example is only a control case.
contract_keywords: Rank Combined QuerySet.none() Branches by Non-Executable Combined State

For the combined-query `.none()` failure, judge paused branches by whether they identify and move toward making the empty clone unable to execute its original combinator operands. Do not give top standing to branches whose main evidence is recursively calling `set_empty()` on `combined_queries`, printing `combined_query[i].is_empty() == True`, or showing ad hoc scripts that happen to return an empty list.

Strong branches should state or implement that the empty clone must have its combined-query execution state cleared, reset, bypassed, or otherwise made non-executable.
If final code is visible, prefer direct code evidence over broad claims.

task_domains: Query pickling diagnosis must trace values_select loss, not just find QuerySet __getstate__

Pre-patch diagnosis of Django issue where pickling queryset.query for values()+annotate queries loses values_select, causing unpickled queries to return broken model instances with AttributeError instead of dicts.
contract_keywords: Query pickling diagnosis must trace values_select loss, not just find QuerySet __getstate__

When diagnosing a Django bug where pickled values()/values_list() querysets return broken model instances instead of dicts, do not reward an agent for merely finding QuerySet.__getstate__/__setstate__ methods in query.py. The critical diagnostic evidence is whether the agent identifies values_select as the lost state in sql/query.py and investigates Query class pickling behavior. Finding pickling methods without reproducing the bug or connecting to values_select loss must score below agents who identify values_select and trace the Query pickling mechanism.

Pre-patch diagnosis of Django issue where pickling queryset.query for values()+annotate queries loses values_select, causing unpickled queries to return broken model instances with AttributeError instead of dicts.

Positive evidence: Agent searches for and identifies values_select in django/db/models/sql/query.py as the attribute controlling dict-vs-instance result types; agent discovers Query class (sql/query.py) has no __getstate__/__setstate__/__reduce__ methods, revealing default pickling behavior; agent traces values() through _values() to set_values() code path where values_select is set; agent reproduces the AttributeError from unpickled query.

Positive evidence: Agent searches for and identifies values_select in django/db/models/sql/query.py as the attribute controlling dict-vs-instance result types; agent discovers Query class (sql/query.py) has no __getstate__/__setstate__/__reduce__ methods, revealing default pickling behavior; agent traces values() through _values() to set_values() code path where values_select is set; agent reproduces the AttributeError from unpickled query.

Contradictory evidence: Agent finds QuerySet.__getstate__/__setstate__ in query.py but does not mention values_select; agent does not reproduce the bug; agent repeats the same grep command (e.g., searching for pickle/__reduce__/__getstate__/__setstate__ twice) without converging; agent examines Prefetch.__getstate__ which is unrelated to Query pickling.

task_domains: Reproduction matching expected output must not overshadow root cause analysis identifying the fix location

Multiple branches diagnose a bug where pickling queryset.query loses values_select, causing ValuesIterable to be replaced by ModelIterable after unpickling. One branch successfully reproduces the bug with exact output matching the issue description (dict before pickling, model instance after, AttributeError on pk access) but then only begins examining _iterable_class without identifying the root cause or fix location. Another branch identifies that the fix should be in the QuerySet query setter, checking values_select to determine _iterable_class and _fields, but has no working reproduction. A third branch examines QuerySet __getstate__ and values_select references, understanding that the QuerySet doesn't use values_select to determine iterable class after unpickling.

task_domains: Variable-poisoning fix: adapt into temp before consuming operation, commit after success — not after the operation

Applies in middleware loading, pipeline construction, handler-chain building, or similar code where a variable is adapted before being passed to a factory that may reject it via an exception. If the main variable is overwritten with the adapted value before the factory call and the factory raises, the chain is poisoned: subsequent iterations receive an incompatibly adapted value. The fix must ensure the operation receives the adapted value while the main variable retains its original value on exception. This is most useful at implementation or review stage when the diff is visible. It is less useful when the trajectory is still exploring or when the diff is not visible in the paused judge view.
contract_keywords: Variable-poisoning fix: adapt into temp before consuming operation, commit after success — not after the operation

Retrieve when evaluating a fix for variable poisoning where a value is adapted (e.g., wrapped for async/sync compatibility) and then passed to an operation (e.g., factory or constructor) that may raise an exception requiring the original unadapted value to be preserved for subsequent iterations. The correct pattern adapts into a temporary variable before the operation, passes the temp to the operation, and only commits the temp to the main variable after the operation succeeds. Moving the adaptation call after the operation is incorrect because it gives the operation the unadapted value.

task_domains: Cap unverified source edits below concrete reproduction work for subtle query-semantics bugs

Applies to tasks where the bug is a semantic mismatch in generated queries or lookup behavior, such as a regular calendar-year optimization being incorrectly applied to ISO-year filtering. At an early pause, a branch may have an untracked reproduction script and environment setup attempts, while another may have a small source edit but no successful run and no visible final diff content. In this situation, source-change presence is only weak evidence: it may be a lucky or wrong edit. A targeted reproduction artifact that encodes the failing query and works toward execution is stronger observable evidence of future success than an unsupported implementation claim. Pure browsing of files, backends, or tests without either a reproduction artifact, a clear diagnosis, or a visible correct patch should remain low-scoring. Absence of completed tests alone is not a flaw when no branch has reached a verified state.
contract_keywords: Cap unverified source edits below concrete reproduction work for subtle query-semantics bugs

Use when judging early trajectories for a subtle query/compiler/lookup semantics defect where no branch has yet produced passing verification, and the visible set contains both speculative source edits and concrete reproduction or test-harness work. The rubric portfolio must not let a non-empty diff, plausible file name, or confident narration dominate the ranking unless the final patch content or execution output directly supports correctness. Reward direct final-state evidence that the branch is making the failure observable.

task_domains: FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME redirect fix must not break URL resolution when path is dual-use

Applies in Django codebases when the task involves FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME not being preserved in admin redirects, specifically in catch_all_view or analogous functions that both resolve URLs and construct redirects. The key visible signal is that the same path variable feeds both resolve() (which expects path_info without SCRIPT_NAME) and HttpResponsePermanentRedirect (which needs path with SCRIPT_NAME). Activate when the visible code shows resolve() usage in the same function as the redirect construction. Do not apply when the function only constructs a redirect without URL resolution, or when the visible prefix does not show resolve() usage.
contract_keywords: FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME redirect fix must not break URL resolution when path is dual-use

Use when a Django admin catch_all_view or similar redirect bug involves FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME and the visible code shows the path variable used for both resolve() and redirect construction. The naive path_info→path replacement breaks URL resolution and must not be rewarded as the correct fix.

task_domains: Weigh Code-Level Mechanism Identification Against Reproduction Success in Pre-Patch Diagnosis Scoring

A Django bug diagnosis task where BoundWidget.id_for_label ignores the id set by ChoiceWidget.create_option. Multiple branches attempted pre-patch diagnosis with varying reproduction success and mechanism identification depth. The rubric explicitly values three dimensions: reproduction, mechanism identification (create_option sets correct id, id_for_label ignores it), and fix localization (BoundWidget.id_for_label in boundfield.py).
contract_keywords: Weigh Code-Level Mechanism Identification Against Reproduction Success in Pre-Patch Diagnosis Scoring

When scoring diagnosis-quality rubrics that include mechanism identification as a component, do not reduce a branch to 'stuck on dependencies' when it has already examined the relevant source code and articulated the causal mechanism in its reasoning. A failed reproduction script does not erase prior code-level diagnosis visible in the paused state. Conversely, successful reproduction output without explicit causal-chain articulation should not receive full marks when the rubric values mechanism identification.

task_domains: Core implementation requirement must match explicit task specification before layering validation criteria

Applies when the task text contains an explicit code snippet showing the desired implementation, such as 'By changing the code to ... def method(self): return expression'. The rubric generation may be tempted to add comprehensive edge-case validation (e.g., testing configurations where a dictionary is empty, requiring fallback behavior, testing unrelated methods) that inadvertently contradicts the explicit specification. The error pattern is that the rubric invents a fallback or compatibility requirement the specification explicitly excludes, causing correct solutions matching the spec to be penalized and wrong solutions adding the invented behavior to be rewarded. This is most relevant when the specification also explicitly states what is NOT in scope (e.g., 'This has nothing to do with method X'). It is less applicable when the specification does not show an exact implementation, when the specification is ambiguous about fallback behavior, or when the task is primarily about adding tests after an already-correct implementation.

task_domains: Guard-clause rubric alignment outweighs comprehensive validation when patch structure shows restructuring

Evaluating continuations for a RenameModel db_table noop fix where the rubric describes adding a guard clause checking original_attrs. Two continuations have patches: one with 3 insertions only (matching rubric's additive description) and one with 7 insertions/6 deletions (restructuring). The restructured patch shows comprehensive validation (table preserved, FK correct, M2M unaffected) while the additive patch's comprehensive test fails with a test infrastructure error.
contract_keywords: Guard-clause rubric alignment outweighs comprehensive validation when patch structure shows restructuring

When a rubric specifies an additive guard-clause fix and one continuation shows comprehensive validation of all contract behaviors but has a patch with significant deletions (restructuring), while another has a minimal additive patch matching the rubric but less comprehensive validation, the judge must weigh patch structure alignment with the rubric over validation output completeness. Restructured patches with deletions are more likely to break edge cases not covered by visible validation scripts.

Positive evidence: A patch with insertions only (no deletions) that matches the rubric's description of 'adding a guard clause' or 'adding a conditional' is strong evidence of correct implementation, even if validation is less comprehensive.

Contradictory evidence: Comprehensive validation outputs showing all three contract behaviors working (table preserved, FK references correct table, M2M tables unaffected) can be misleading when the patch has significant deletions indicating restructuring rather than a simple guard clause addition.

Explicitly reject the pattern of using comprehensive validation outputs as the primary scoring signal when the patch structure (diff_stat with deletions) contradicts the rubric's additive description.

A Django JSONField bug where has_key/has_keys/has_any_keys fail for numeric keys on SQLite. The fix adds a force_string_keys parameter to compile_json_path. Multiple continuations attempt to validate by running tests but all fail to configure the test environment. One continuation (s04) shows the modified function signature via grep, another (s00) shows only ls/find and a failing django test command with no patch visible, and a third (s06) shows the original function then applies a sed fix at the very last step.
contract_keywords: Visible Modified Source Outweighs Failed Test-Setup Commands for Validation Evidence Scoring

When all continuations fail to execute tests, a branch showing the modified source code (e.g., a new function parameter in grep/sed output) provides stronger validation evidence than a branch that merely invokes failing test commands from the checkout root. Failed test-setup commands (RuntimeError, ImproperlyConfigured, ModuleNotFoundError) are evidence of validation failure, not validation success. Do not rank a continuation higher because it uses /testbed paths if no patch is visible and every test command returns a traceback.

task_domains: SQLite Reproduction Cannot Validate PostgreSQL-Specific Constraint Collision Fix

The issue reports that dropping a unique_together constraint on a primary key field fails on PostgreSQL because the schema editor's _delete_composed_index method finds two unique constraints (the primary key and the unique_together) and expects only one. The fix must disambiguate these constraints by excluding primary key constraints when searching for unique_together constraints to delete. The rubrics require reproduction of the exact migration failure scenario with clear before/after constraint evidence.
contract_keywords: SQLite Reproduction Cannot Validate PostgreSQL-Specific Constraint Collision Fix

When a bug report describes a PostgreSQL-specific constraint behavior where primary keys are also marked as unique, a reproduction test running on SQLite that prints 'SUCCESS' does not validate the fix. On SQLite, primary key constraints have unique=False, so the dual-constraint collision (primary key + unique_together on the same column) never occurs. A migration removing unique_together on a primary key field will succeed on SQLite even without any code changes. Do not credit reproduction evidence that runs on a different database backend than the one in the bug report, especially when constraint introspection output from the same trajectory shows the bug condition is absent on that backend.

task_domains: Implementation Contract Preservation Over Test-Activity Displacement

In a task adding transaction handling to admin changelist processing, continuations diverged in the validation phase: one reverted the modified file by copying a .bak backup over it, one ran partial test diagnostics showing captured query output, and one installed the project in editable mode to enable test execution. The biased rubric scored the patch-reverting and partial-test continuations equally, above the environment-setup continuation, because test-activity and transaction-pattern criteria displaced the all-or-nothing requirement that the implementation change remain intact.
contract_keywords: Implementation Contract Preservation Over Test-Activity Displacement

When scoring continuations of a code-modification task, the preservation of the implementation patch is the primary contract and must not be displaced by test-validation or pattern-matching criteria. A continuation that reverts the patch by restoring a backup copy destroys the implementation and must receive the lowest score regardless of preceding test-exploration activity. A continuation that takes constructive environment-setup steps to enable the test infrastructure while preserving the patch should not be outranked by continuations showing only partial test diagnostics.

task_domains: Read Test Command Outcomes Before Crediting Validation

Applies in SWE-agent trajectories at the validation or final-review stage when the agent runs test commands (e.g., a project test runner, `python -m django test`, `python -m pytest`) and the rubric awards credit for test-suite execution, failure-mode reproduction, or regression verification. It is most useful when test commands can fail noisily but superficially resemble test activity—wrong test class names produce 'unittest.loader._FailedTest', missing settings produce 'ImproperlyConfigured', wrong paths produce 'ModuleNotFoundError', and zero-test runs print 'OK' with 'Ran 0 tests'. It is less useful when no test commands appear in the visible prefix, or when the rubric concerns only code inspection rather than test execution.
contract_keywords: Read Test Command Outcomes Before Crediting Validation

The judge must parse the actual output to determine whether tests passed or failed, rather than crediting the mere invocation of a named test command.

task_domains: Redundant Testing Rubrics Amplify Proxy Validation Over Targeted Fix Verification

Software engineering evaluation often assesses testing discipline through multiple rubrics: running existing test suites, exercising specific test commands, running extended suites, verifying behavioral contracts, and isolating pre-existing failures. While each appears distinct, they frequently overlap in practice—a continuation running the project test suite and exercising specific commands both validate 'did the agent verify the fix against tests.' When these rubrics are weighted and summed, a continuation performing broad testing accumulates credit across all overlapping rubrics, inflating its score relative to a continuation that writes a targeted test for the specific behavior the fix addresses. Do not create multiple rubrics that all reward the same underlying testing activity; if rubrics overlap, consolidate them or reduce individual weights so their combined weight does not exceed rubrics measuring fix correctness.
contract_keywords: Redundant Testing Rubrics Amplify Proxy Validation Over Targeted Fix Verification

When a rubric set contains multiple rubrics that reward overlapping testing and validation activities, their combined weight can cause a continuation that performs broad but non-targeted testing to outscore one that performs targeted verification of the specific behavior the fix is meant to correct. The judge must ensure that overlapping testing rubrics do not collectively overshadow rubrics measuring actual fix correctness, and that a continuation's score reflects the relevance of its testing to the fix, not merely the quantity of test commands executed.

A continuation performing both broad and targeted testing legitimately earns credit across all rubrics—do not penalize thoroughness.

A FileResponse fix requires adding content_type dictionary entries for 'br' and 'compress' encodings in set_headers. Multiple branches applied 2-line sed edits to the response file. The visible edit commands reveal the exact MIME type strings used, which determine correctness. The rubric listed both application/brotli and application/x-brotli as acceptable, but only application/x-brotli is correct.
contract_keywords: Distinguish application/x-brotli from application/brotli in MIME type mapping fixes

When evaluating fixes that add brotli MIME type mappings, application/x-brotli and application/brotli are not interchangeable. Only application/x-brotli is the correct MIME type for the br encoding. Branches using application/brotli must be scored lower than branches using application/x-brotli, regardless of surrounding validation activity or post-edit code display.

A FileResponse fix requires adding content_type dictionary entries for 'br' and 'compress' encodings in set_headers. Multiple branches applied 2-line sed edits to the response file. Positive evidence: The visible sed or edit command inserts "br": "application/x-brotli" into the content_type dictionary alongside "compress": "application/x-compress".
Contradictory evidence: The visible sed or edit command inserts "br": "application/brotli" (missing the x- prefix).

The order of dictionary entries (br first vs compress first) does not affect correctness; branches with different ordering but the same MIME type values are equivalent implementations and should receive the same score.

task_domains: Codebase Naming Convention Should Override Rubric's MIME Type Standard Claim

A FileResponse fix adds br (brotli) and compress (.Z) encoding mappings to a dictionary that already contains bzip2 -> application/x-bzip, gzip -> application/gzip, and xz -> application/x-xz. Two implementation branches differ only in the brotli MIME type: one uses application/brotli (IANA standard), the other uses application/x-brotli (matching the application/x- prefix convention of existing entries). Both branches correctly map compress -> application/x-compress. Both implementations are structurally equivalent: same file, same method, same dictionary, same number of entries added.
contract_keywords: Codebase Naming Convention Should Override Rubric's MIME Type Standard Claim

When a fix adds new MIME type entries to an existing encoding-to-MIME-type dictionary, the new entries should follow the naming convention of existing entries. A rubric may incorrectly assert that an IANA-standard MIME type is 'correct' while labeling the codebase-consistent vendor-prefixed type as 'legacy,' leading to inverted scoring where the convention-consistent branch is penalized.

Positive evidence: The branch using application/x-brotli maintains naming consistency with the existing dictionary: application/x-bzip (bzip2), application/x-xz (xz), and application/x-compress (compress) all use the application/x- prefix.

A rubric may incorrectly assert that an IANA-standard MIME type is 'correct' while labeling the codebase-consistent vendor-prefixed type as 'legacy,' leading to inverted scoring where the convention-consistent branch is penalized.

A FileResponse fix adds br (brotli) and compress (.Z) encoding mappings to a dictionary that already contains bzip2 -> application/x-bzip, gzip -> application/gzip, and xz -> application/x-xz. Two implementation branches differ only in the brotli MIME type: one uses application/brotli (IANA standard), the other uses application/x-brotli (matching the application/x- prefix convention of existing entries). Both branches correctly map compress -> application/x-compress. Both implementations are structurally equivalent: same file, same method, same dictionary, same number of entries added.

Positive evidence: The branch using application/x-brotli maintains naming consistency with the existing dictionary: application/x-bzip (bzip2), application/x-xz (xz), and application/x-compress (compress) all use the application/x- prefix.
Contradictory evidence: A rubric may assert that application/brotli is the 'correct standard MIME type' and classify application/x-brotli as a 'legacy vendor-prefixed' type deserving a lower score.
Reject the claim that application/brotli is inherently more correct than application/x-brotli in this context.

The application/gzip entry (without x- prefix) is an exception where the IANA standard happened to match; the majority of existing entries use application/x- prefix, and new entries should follow the majority pattern.

task_domains: Implementation Code Must Drive Correctness Assessment Over Validation Activity for Template Filter Semantics

A new template filter escapeseq is being implemented to escape each element in a sequence before joining. The PR specifies the filter is for use 'in a context where autoescape is off,' so the filter must escape unconditionally regardless of autoescape setting. Two implementation approaches are visible: (1) using conditional_escape without needs_autoescape (always escapes, correct), and (2) using needs_autoescape=True with an autoescape guard that only escapes when autoescape is on (buggy, fails the PR's autoescape-off use case).
contract_keywords: Implementation Code Must Drive Correctness Assessment Over Validation Activity for Template Filter Semantics

When evaluating template filter implementations, the actual filter code visible via diff and code inspection must be the primary correctness signal. Validation activity (test files, test suite runs, PR example verification) is secondary and must not override implementation analysis. Nodes with identical diffs have identical implementations and must receive equivalent correctness scores regardless of validation breadth.

task_domains: Do not reward test file inclusion in submitted patches as complete deliverables

A template filter implementation task where multiple continuations produce correct implementations but differ in whether they include test files in the submitted patch. Some continuations include test files in the submitted patch (appearing as complete deliverables with implementation, documentation, and tests), while others include only source code changes and optionally documentation.
contract_keywords: Do not reward test file inclusion in submitted patches as complete deliverables

Including a test file in the submitted patch causes the solution to fail even when the implementation is correct. The judge should not reward 'complete deliverables' that include test files in the submitted patch. Instead, verify that the submitted patch includes only source code changes and documentation, not test files.

task_domains: Do not reward fix attempts whose own validation proves ineffectiveness — persisted original error overrides correct-layer code pattern

In a Django ORM task where aggregates over window functions produce a database OperationalError, one continuation modifies Aggregate.resolve_expression to check contains_over_clause and raise FieldError — matching the expected fix pattern exactly. However, when it runs the reproduction test afterward, the output still shows the same OperationalError ('misuse of window function SUM()'), proving the fix does not intercept at the right execution point. The judge awarded this continuation the highest score, fooled by the code pattern match, while continuations still debugging received zero.
contract_keywords: Do not reward fix attempts whose own validation proves ineffectiveness — persisted original error overrides correct-layer code pattern

A continuation that modifies the expected file with the expected check and error type still deserves a low score when its own validation run shows the original error persisting unchanged. Visible validation output contradicting the fix's effectiveness must override surface-level code pattern matching.

Contradictory evidence: The continuation's own validation output shows the SAME original error type and message persisting after the fix (e.g., OperationalError still raised instead of the expected FieldError).

A bug fix for hist() not respecting range when density=True. The shared parent trajectory already tested multiple edge cases (multi-dataset arrays, empty data) and performed git-stash regression verification. All continuations submit the identical one-line fix preserving existing kwargs: hist_kwargs = dict(hist_kwargs, density=density).
contract_keywords: Do not rank submission-only continuations by validation breadth when patches are identical and validation was already performed in the shared parent

A validation-breadth rubric misranks continuations that are purely submission steps when all continuations share a parent trajectory that already performed edge-case testing and regression verification. The continuation that adds explicit validation should not score lower than ones that add none.

task_domains: Validate Divider Segment Positions Per Extend Mode, Not Just Segment Counts

Colorbar divider lines are drawn from a LineCollection whose segments are derived by slicing a coordinate mesh array. The original bug excludes the first and last segments via [1:-1] slicing, which removes extension boundary edges. A correct fix must include the appropriate extension boundary segments. However, some fixes may add the wrong boundary segment for a given extend mode — for example, including the upper boundary when only the lower extension is active, or vice versa. This produces the correct segment count but at wrong positions, making the fix functionally incorrect. The rubric must distinguish between 'correct count at wrong positions' and 'correct count at correct positions' by examining the actual printed segment coordinates.
contract_keywords: Validate Divider Segment Positions Per Extend Mode, Not Just Segment Counts

When evaluating colorbar drawedges fixes that modify divider segment selection, the rubric must require verification of actual segment coordinate positions for each extend mode independently. A fix that produces the correct segment count but includes the wrong boundary positions is incorrect. For extend='min', the lower extension boundary segment must be included and the upper outer-edge segment excluded. For extend='max', the upper extension boundary segment must be included and the lower outer-edge segment excluded. For extend='both', both extension boundary segments must be included. A fix that reverses which boundary is included for min versus max is incorrect even if the total segment count matches the expected value for each mode. The rubric must explicitly forbid scoring a fix as correct based on segment count alone without checking which coordinate positions are actually present in the printed divider segments.

Activation: When visible evidence shows divider segment coordinates printed for multiple extend modes (at least min and max tested separately), or when a continuation's diff modifies the segment slicing logic in the divider-setting code path.
Positive evidence: For each extend mode tested, the printed divider segment coordinates include the correct extension boundary and exclude the non-extension outer edge.
Both the count AND the actual coordinate values must be correct.
Contradictory evidence: The segment count matches the expected number for a given extend mode, but the actual coordinate values reveal that the wrong boundary is included.
This must be scored as incorrect regardless of the matching count.
failure_modes: Do not score such a fix as fully correct; it must be penalized for the min/max position errors even if the 'both' case works and all counts match.

Abstention boundary: When the visible evidence only shows segment counts without actual coordinate values, or when only one extend mode is tested, the rubric should not assert that positions are correct.
In such cases, score based on available position evidence only and note that per-mode position validation is incomplete.

When evaluating colorbar drawedges fixes that modify divider segment selection, the rubric must require verification of actual segment coordinate positions for each extend mode independently. A fix that produces the correct segment count but includes the wrong boundary positions is incorrect. For extend='min', the lower extension boundary segment must be included and the upper outer-edge segment excluded. For extend='max', the upper extension boundary segment must be included and the lower outer-edge segment excluded. For extend='both', both extension boundary segments must be included. A fix that reverses which boundary is included for min versus max is incorrect even if the total segment count matches the expected value for each mode. The rubric must explicitly forbid scoring a fix as correct based on segment count alone without checking which coordinate positions are actually present in the printed divider segments.

Colorbar divider lines are drawn from a LineCollection whose segments are derived by slicing a coordinate mesh array. The original bug excludes the first and last segments via [1:-1] slicing, which removes extension boundary edges. A correct fix must include the appropriate extension boundary segments. However, some fixes may add the wrong boundary segment for a given extend mode — for example, including the upper boundary when only the lower extension is active, or vice versa. This produces the correct segment count but at wrong positions, making the fix functionally incorrect. The rubric must distinguish between 'correct count at wrong positions' and 'correct count at correct positions' by examining the actual printed segment coordinates.

Activation: When visible evidence shows divider segment coordinates printed for multiple extend modes (at least min and max tested separately), or when a continuation's diff modifies the segment slicing logic in the divider-setting code path.
Positive evidence: For each extend mode tested, the printed divider segment coordinates include the correct extension boundary and exclude the non-extension outer edge.
Both the count AND the actual coordinate values must be correct.
Contradictory evidence: The segment count matches the expected number for a given extend mode, but the actual coordinate values reveal that the wrong boundary is included.
This must be scored as incorrect regardless of the matching count.

task_domains: Separate false-negative reproduction from root-cause identification; calibrate criteria to visible stage

Applies in SWE-agent diagnosis or exploration trajectories where the reported bug is environment- or backend-specific (e.g., a particular GUI backend, OS, or library version). The misleading case is when a continuation runs the reproduction script and sees a 'successful' or 'no error' output because it used a different backend or version than the bug report, then the judge treats that output as evidence of root-cause understanding or fix validation. Equally misleading is rewarding environment-setup commands (path manipulation, package installation, version checks) as if they were root-cause analysis. The judge must instead look at whether the trajectory recognizes the condition mismatch, attempts to match the reported environment, or investigates the actual code path where the unpicklable or unserializable reference originates.
contract_keywords: Separate false-negative reproduction from root-cause identification; calibrate criteria to visible stage

Use this when a bug report names a specific backend, version, or runtime condition and trajectories show reproduction attempts that may produce false-negative 'success' under mismatched conditions. The core failure mode is a rubric that conflates reproduction output or environment setup with root-cause identification, causing the judge to reward a trajectory that obtained a misleading 'success' over trajectories that actually investigated the failing code path. A second failure mode is a rubric that demands implementation details not yet visible in an exploration-stage prefix, yielding uninformative all-zero scores across all candidates.

That conflation inverts the evidence when the reproduction is a false negative: a trajectory that sees a pass output under a mismatched backend has not identified the root cause and may be worse than a trajectory that fails to reproduce but correctly investigates the source code.

A better rubric should: (1) treat any 'success' output obtained under conditions that do not match the bug report as a false negative requiring further investigation, not as positive evidence; (2) explicitly decline to reward environment-setup commands as root-cause progress; (3) score root-cause evidence from reading the actual class or function where the reported unpicklable reference is stored, recognizing pickle-state customization patterns, or recognizing the backend or version mismatch; (4) calibrate scale anchors to what is visible at the current trajectory stage so that exploration-stage prefixes are not scored against implementation completeness they cannot yet show.

task_domains: Cross-Path Bug Discovery Outweighs Same-Path Test Volume in Multi-Path Fix Validation

A seaborn legend offset issue where large numbers (order 1E6) show wrong legend labels because the ScalarFormatter offset is not applied. The issue explicitly states both so.Plot (via scales.py Continuous._legend) and sns.scatterplot (via utils.py locator_to_legend_entries) are affected. Fixes that only modify scales.py leave the scatterplot path unfixed. Edge cases include negative values (Unicode minus '−' vs ASCII '-' causing float() conversion failure) and math text format offsets (LaTeX like '$\times\mathdefault{10^{6}}$' vs '1e6').
contract_keywords: Cross-Path Bug Discovery Outweighs Same-Path Test Volume in Multi-Path Fix Validation

When an issue affects two distinct code paths and a fix addresses only one, a continuation that tests the unfixed path and discovers it still fails provides stronger validation evidence than one that runs multiple passing tests on the already-fixed path. Do not let the quantity of successful same-path tests obscure the diagnostic value of a cross-path failure discovery or an edge case crash.

Positive evidence: A continuation that tests the unfixed code path and discovers it still produces wrong output demonstrates that the fix is incomplete.

For example, testing sns.scatterplot and finding legend labels show '3.0, 3.6, 4.2, 4.8, 5.4, 6.0' instead of true values like '3000000' is strong validation evidence that the scales.py-only fix is incomplete.

Contradictory evidence: A continuation may show multiple successful test scenarios on the fixed path — so.Plot with large numbers producing labels ['3000000.0', '4000000.0', '5000000.0', '6000000.0'], additive offset cases producing correct absolute labels, and small number cases all passing.

While this demonstrates the fix works for the tested path, it does not validate the unfixed path and should not be scored higher than a continuation that discovered the cross-path failure or edge case crash.

task_domains: Deprecation-aware API parameter rename with backward compatibility

Applies in Python library maintenance when the issue or task text explicitly mentions deprecation cycles, backward compatibility, or similar transition concerns for a public parameter rename. The decisive activation signal is the task asking whether a deprecation cycle is required or whether old callers will break. This is most useful once the trajectory has begun investigating deprecation utilities, examining how existing callers use the old parameter, or editing the target method. It should not be applied when the task explicitly permits a breaking change, when no compatibility concern is raised in the task text, or when the parameter being renamed is internal or private with no external callers.
contract_keywords: Deprecation-aware API parameter rename with backward compatibility

Use when a task requires renaming a public method parameter and the task text explicitly raises whether a deprecation cycle is needed, signaling that existing callers of the old parameter name must continue to work during the transition period.

The rubric must not reduce the task to a direct parameter rename that achieves surface-level API consistency.

A direct rename that removes the old parameter name entirely breaks existing callers and should not be rewarded as complete or correct, even if the method signature, docstring, and internal call all consistently use the new name.

Positive evidence includes: investigation of the project's deprecation or alias utilities (e.g., functions that emit deprecation warnings, alias message helpers, FutureWarning usage patterns), examination of how existing tests or callers invoke the old parameter name, planning or implementing dual-name support where the old name still works with a warning, and updating internal calls to use the new canonical name.

Contradictory evidence includes: a clean direct rename of the parameter in signature, docstring, and internal call with no deprecation handling whatsoever, no investigation of how existing callers use the old parameter, or removal of the old parameter without any transition mechanism.
Do not reward this as complete solely because it achieves API consistency on the surface.

A trajectory that directly renames the parameter without any deprecation handling should score no higher than a trajectory that has not yet made changes but is investigating deprecation patterns.

task_domains: Do not reward inherited patch maturity over contract-grounded tracing

Applies in multi-round code-repair trajectories where branches can inherit patches from prior rounds. The misleading case is when an inherited patch passes local validation and appears mature, leading the judge to score it higher, while sibling branches that are still tracing the mechanism (e.g., how attributes are collected, what type-filtering functions return, how a callback receives its arguments) are scored as if they were failing. The inherited patch can be wrong on the specific contract even though it runs without error, and the tracing branches may be building the understanding needed for a correct fix. This is especially dangerous when the inherited patch's own validation output reveals the contract violation (e.g., the wrong source's attributes appearing in the result) but the judge treats test passage as sufficient.
contract_keywords: Do not reward inherited patch maturity over contract-grounded tracing

The inherited modification may look settled and pass local tests but still violate the task's specific behavioral contract.

task_domains: Judge xarray timedelta64 polyval repairs by call-path readiness and branch preservation

Activation: use when the task report shows `xr.polyval` producing huge values for a timedelta64 coordinate and the trajectory is paused around diagnosis-to-fix transition. Positive evidence includes inspecting the actual `_ensure_numeric` implementation that passes an epoch-like datetime offset into `datetime_to_numeric`, testing the failing timedelta64 conversion on the MVCE coordinate or through the `_ensure_numeric`/`to_floatable` path, and explicitly preserving the intended datetime64 behavior while changing only the timedelta64 handling. Strong trajectories may use `None`, a zero timedelta offset, or another equivalent type-compatible approach for relative durations, but they should not collapse both dtype kinds into one unexamined rule.
contract_keywords: Judge xarray timedelta64 polyval repairs by call-path readiness and branch preservation

Retrieve for this xarray `polyval` regression when the visible trajectory has found `_ensure_numeric`, `datetime_to_numeric`, or the `datetime64`/`timedelta64` offset interaction. The diagnostic rule is: do not give implementation-level credit merely for a polished explanation or an isolated conversion demo. Prefer trajectories that visibly connect the timedelta64 offset finding back to the active `_ensure_numeric`/`to_floatable` code path in `xarray/core/computation.py`, identify the two dtype branches that need different semantics, and are positioned to make a branch-preserving repair.

Activation: use when the task report shows `xr.polyval` producing huge values for a timedelta64 coordinate and the trajectory is paused around diagnosis-to-fix transition. Positive evidence includes inspecting the actual `_ensure_numeric` implementation that passes an epoch-like datetime offset into `datetime_to_numeric`, testing the failing timedelta64 conversion on the MVCE coordinate or through the `_ensure_numeric`/`to_floatable` path, and explicitly preserving the intended datetime64 behavior while changing only the timedelta64 handling. Strong trajectories may use `None`, a zero timedelta offset, or another equivalent type-compatible approach for relative durations, but they should not collapse both dtype kinds into one unexamined rule.

A trajectory that says the epoch offset is wrong for timedelta64 and demonstrates `datetime_to_numeric` returning `[0, 1e10, 2e10, ...]` has useful diagnostic evidence, but that alone should not outrank a trajectory that also inspects or exercises `_ensure_numeric`/`to_floatable` and is about to modify that exact branch.

Conversely, a trajectory that proposes using `offset=None` uniformly for both datetime64 and timedelta64 should be treated as contradictory evidence unless it also explains why existing datetime64 behavior is preserved; testing `offset=None` on datetime64 and observing relative-to-min values is not validation of the desired branch-preserving behavior.

Close-looking exclusions: do not reward work on Horner's method, coefficient ordering, dimension transposition, or broad `polyval` rewrites as if they fixed the dtype conversion issue; do not treat merely reading existing tests or git history as stronger than evidence tied to the active conversion branch.

Activation: use when the task report shows `xr.polyval` producing huge values for a timedelta64 coordinate and the trajectory is paused around diagnosis-to-fix transition. Positive evidence includes inspecting the actual `_ensure_numeric` implementation that passes an epoch-like datetime offset into `datetime_to_numeric`, testing the failing timedelta64 conversion on the MVCE coordinate or through the `_ensure_numeric`/`to_floatable` path, and explicitly preserving the intended datetime64 behavior while changing only the timedelta64 handling. Strong trajectories may use `None`, a zero timedelta offset, or another equivalent type-compatible approach for relative durations, but they should not collapse both dtype kinds into one unexamined rule.

Close-looking exclusions: do not reward work on Horner's method, coefficient ordering, dimension transposition, or broad `polyval` rewrites as if they fixed the dtype conversion issue; do not treat merely reading existing tests or git history as stronger than evidence tied to the active conversion branch.

task_domains: Distinguish checked-out source paths from installed site-packages when scoring source-level validation rubrics

In Python package development environments, the checked-out source version (e.g., a dev build) often differs from the globally installed package version (e.g., a newer release). A trajectory that validates against the installed package may appear to succeed while the checked-out source remains unfixed. The judge must not conflate exploring the installed package to understand a serialization contract with validating the fix against the checked-out source.

task_domains: Validation Test Failures Must Outrank Minimal Diff Size and Reproduction Success

Evaluating fixes for a StratifiedKFold shuffle bug where per-class KFold instances share the same random_state, producing identical fold pairs regardless of seed. The correct fix derives independent per-class random states from the base random_state in _make_test_folds. Multiple continuations apply patches of varying scope and run validation tests with different outcomes.
contract_keywords: Validation Test Failures Must Outrank Minimal Diff Size and Reproduction Success

When a fix shows positive reproduction output (different fold pairs across random seeds) but its own validation test crashes with a concrete error, the validation failure must dominate the fix quality score. Do not let minimal diff size or basic reproduction success override a visible validation test failure.

Activation: When a trajectory shows both reproduction output indicating the bug is addressed (different fold pairs across random seeds) AND a validation test run in the same trajectory, the validation test outcome must be checked before scoring fix quality.

Positive evidence: A fix that (a) modifies _make_test_folds to derive independent per-class random states from the base random_state, (b) shows different fold pairs in reproduction output, AND (c) runs validation that confirms stratification is preserved with per-fold class counts visible in output (e.g., multi-class test showing balanced train/test splits across 3+ classes).

Contradictory evidence: A fix that shows different fold pairs in reproduction output BUT its validation test fails with a concrete error (e.g., 'ValueError: Found input variables with inconsistent numbers of samples: [100, 99]').
This validation failure must reduce the fix quality score below any fix whose validation passes, regardless of diff size or reproduction success.

Close-looking exclusion: A broader diff (e.g., 37 insertions, 28 deletions) that includes visible multi-class stratification verification (per-fold class counts showing balanced splits across 3+ classes) should not be penalized below a minimal diff (e.g., 11 insertions, 3 deletions) whose validation test crashed.
failure_modes: 'Minimal in scope' means no unnecessary changes to other files or methods, not 'smallest possible diff.' Comprehensive validation with a moderately broader diff is stronger evidence of correctness than minimalism with a failing test.

Close-looking exclusion: A fix where sed editing produced duplicated code blocks (both the new per-class random state derivation and the original per_cls_cvs assignment visible in the file) should be penalized for the duplication bug even if the diff appears to contain correct logic.

task_domains: Do not reward fix attempts that are subsequently reverted via git checkout

Two trajectories diagnosed an IndexError in tree export_text with a single feature. Both located the exact failing line (feature_names_ = [feature_names[i] for i in tree_.feature]) and identified the TREE_UNDEFINED (-2) sentinel mechanism: leaf nodes carry TREE_UNDEFINED in tree_.feature, and with a single-element feature_names list, index -2 is out of range. One trajectory applied a correct guard (i != _tree.TREE_UNDEFINED) via sed and verified the code change, but then ran `git checkout sklearn/tree/export.py` to revert all changes. The other showed equivalent diagnosis without reverting. The judge gave the reverting trajectory a higher score, misled by the visible fix attempt.
contract_keywords: Do not reward fix attempts that are subsequently reverted via git checkout

The visible fix attempt in intermediate steps is misleading evidence of progress. Such a trajectory should not score higher than one with equivalent root-cause diagnosis that retains its changes or shows no revert.

The visible fix attempt in intermediate steps is misleading evidence of progress. Such a trajectory should not score higher than one with equivalent root-cause diagnosis that retains its changes or shows no revert.

Two trajectories diagnosed an IndexError in tree export_text with a single feature. Both located the exact failing line (feature_names_ = [feature_names[i] for i in tree_.feature]) and identified the TREE_UNDEFINED (-2) sentinel mechanism: leaf nodes carry TREE_UNDEFINED in tree_.feature, and with a single-element feature_names list, index -2 is out of range. One trajectory applied a correct guard (i != _tree.TREE_UNDEFINED) via sed and verified the code change, but then ran `git checkout sklearn/tree/export.py` to revert all changes. The other showed equivalent diagnosis without reverting. The judge gave the reverting trajectory a higher score, misled by the visible fix attempt.

Positive evidence: A trajectory that locates the exact failing line, explains the sentinel mechanism (TREE_UNDEFINED = -2 for leaf nodes, feature_names[-2] out of range with 1 feature), and either retains its changes or shows no revert demonstrates complete diagnosis.

Two trajectories with equivalent diagnosis depth—both tracing tree_.feature through leaf-node sentinels to the IndexError—should receive equivalent diagnosis scores regardless of whether one additionally wrote and then discarded a fix.
Contradictory evidence: A trajectory that applies a correct fix but then runs `git checkout sklearn/tree/export.py` has no final patch.
This must not earn a higher diagnosis score than equivalent diagnosis without the revert.
The `git checkout` command targeting the fixed file is definitive evidence that the fix was discarded, and the trajectory's final state is no better than one that never attempted a fix at all.

task_domains: Require Visible Patch Evidence Before Scoring Code-Fix Rubrics

Judges evaluating code-fix rubrics at paused states may encounter agents that have investigated the codebase (read files, run reproductions) but have not yet written a patch. The judge must distinguish investigation from modification. A visible diff is the only reliable evidence of a code fix; reading files and running scripts are investigation. Reproduction output when no patch exists reflects the current codebase's behavior, not the agent's modifications.
contract_keywords: Require Visible Patch Evidence Before Scoring Code-Fix Rubrics

When no patch is visible in a paused state, code-fix rubrics must not receive positive scores for source-file reading alone, and fix-quality penalties must not be inferred from reproduction output that reflects the current codebase rather than the agent's changes.
